source SVG inspection tasks: Do not award task credit for merely parsing the unchanged input SVG; use the source only as expected data for validating user-created artifacts so the initial state receives zero reward.
plain-text exact line count: When an instruction requires exactly two lines, evaluate physical lines after normal newline normalization rather than filtering to non-empty lines, otherwise files with extra blank lines can incorrectly pass.
SVG group and stroke verification: For SVG tasks requiring exactly one group, count all <g> elements in the document, not just groups matching the target children; Inkscape files may contain extra layer or stale groups. Also explicitly validate 'no stroke' via stroke:none/absent/transparent or zero stroke-width.
SVG grouping verification: Inkscape layers are saved as <g inkscape:groupmode="layer"> elements, so an evaluator must distinguish layer groups from user-created groups; otherwise ungrouped objects on the default layer can falsely satisfy a '<g> wraps shapes' check.
SVG group verification: For exact-structure SVG tasks, do not only count the required child tags; also reject extra graphical elements and be explicit about whether Inkscape layer <g> wrappers are allowed, because tolerating layer groups can conflict with an instruction requiring exactly one <g> element.
SVG shape verification: For SVG drawing tasks, in addition to checking element tags and styles, verify visible geometry such as rect width/height > 0 and ellipse rx/ry or circle r > 0, and consider display/visibility/opacity to avoid accepting invisible placeholder elements.
dependency-chain source parsing: Do not award independent rule credit for static source/input files that exist before the task; parse them only to compute expected output values, otherwise preflight can get positive reward without user action.
SVG viewBox-derived dimensions: When output dimensions depend on source SVG viewBox values, a stronger evaluator can parse the source SVG root viewBox directly and compute expected dimensions instead of hardcoding them.
SVG attribute handoff verification: For tasks that ask the user to transcribe SVG root attributes into a text file, parsing the source SVG should provide expected values but should not itself award reward; otherwise the initial state can receive positive credit before the output artifact exists.
dependency-derived expected values: When an output must be derived from an existing input file, parse the input to compute expected values inside the verification, but do not assign a separate reward for the unchanged input file; otherwise the initial state can receive positive score.
